023/**
024 * Describes a key (or several fallback keys) resolved against a {@link LogProperties}
025 * instance - start with {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} - and also serves as the
026 * namespace for the shared property machinery: {@link Result}, {@link Validator}, and the
027 * property-specific exceptions.
028 *
029 * @see LogProperties
030 */
031@CaseChanging
032public interface LogProperty {
033
034        /**
035         * The first key tried.
036         * @return key.
037         */
038        public String key();
039
040        /**
041         * Every key tried, in order - the first key given to
042         * {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)}/{@link LogProperties#forKey(String, String)}
043         * followed by any added via {@link #or(String)}/{@link #or(String, String)}.
044         * @return keys.
045         */
046        public List<String> keys();
047
048        /**
049         * The properties this key (or keys) will be looked up against.
050         * @return properties.
051         */
052        public LogProperties properties();
053
054        /**
055         * Resolves the property as a raw string.
056         * @return result.
057         */
058        public Result<String> ofString();
059
060        /**
061         * Resolves the property as a list, using {@link LogProperties#listOrNull(String)}.
062         * @return result.
063         */
064        public Result<List<String>> ofList();
065
066        /**
067         * Resolves the property as a map, using {@link LogProperties#mapOrNull(String)}.
068         * @return result.
069         */
070        public Result<Map<String, String>> ofMap();
071
072        /**
073         * Parses a case-insensitive enum value and reports the valid property values when
074         * parsing fails. Enum names and additional values are shown in lowercase, as property
075         * values conventionally are.
076         * @param <E> enum type.
077         * @param enumType enum class.
078         * @param value input value.
079         * @param additionalValues accepted aliases or other values supported by the property.
080         * @return parsed enum value.
081         */
082        static <E extends Enum<E>> E enumValue(Class<E> enumType, String value, String... additionalValues) {
083                try {
084                        return Enum.valueOf(enumType, value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
085                }
086                catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
087                        var available = new LinkedHashSet<String>();
088                        EnumSet.allOf(enumType).stream().map(v -> v.name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)).forEach(available::add);
089                        Arrays.stream(additionalValues).map(v -> v.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)).forEach(available::add);
090                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("'" + value + "' is not a valid value for " + enumType.getCanonicalName()
091                                        + ". Valid values: " + String.join(", ", available.stream().map(v -> "'" + v + "'").toList()), e);
092                }
093        }
094
095        /**
096         * Resolves the property as an int.
097         * @return result.
098         */
099        default Result<Integer> ofInt() {
100                return ofString().map(Integer::parseInt);
101        }
102
103        /**
104         * Resolves the property as a long.
105         * @return result.
106         */
107        default Result<Long> ofLong() {
108                return ofString().map(Long::parseLong);
109        }
110
111        /**
112         * Resolves the property as a boolean.
113         * <p>
114         * {@link Boolean#parseBoolean(String)} treats any value other than
115         * <code>"true"</code> (case-insensitive) as <code>false</code> - a typo or a
116         * reasonable-looking alternative like <code>someFlag=yes</code> silently resolves to
117         * <code>false</code> instead of failing loudly. Component/plugin authors implementing
118         * a new property should prefer a small enum (with
119         * <code>true</code>/<code>false</code> aliased to e.g.
120         * <code>on</code>/<code>off</code> members) parsed via {@link #ofString()} instead,
121         * so a bad value alerts rather than silently resolving false. This method remains
122         * available (and fine) for end users setting an existing boolean property.
123         * @return result.
124         */
125        default Result<Boolean> ofBoolean() {
126                return ofString().map(Boolean::parseBoolean);
127        }
128
129        /**
130         * Resolves the property as a URI.
131         * @return result.
132         */
133        default Result<URI> ofURI() {
134                return ofString().map(URI::new);
135        }
136
137        /**
138         * Resolves the property as a {@link LogProviderRef} for component provision.
139         * @return result.
140         * @see LogOutput#of(LogProviderRef)
141         */
142        default Result<LogProviderRef> ofProviderRef() {
143                return switch (ofURI()) {
144                        case Result.Success<URI> s -> mapValue(s, LogProviderRef.of(s.value(), s.key()));
145                        case Result.Missing<URI> m -> m.convert();
146                        case Result.Error<URI> e -> e.convert();
147                };
148        }
149
150        /**
151         * Resolves the property as a {@link LogProviderRef} and then maps it to a
152         * {@link LogProvider}.
153         * @param <U> provider type.
154         * @param mapper function to map to provider.
155         * @return result.
156         * @see LogOutput#of(LogProviderRef)
157         */
158        default <U> Result<LogProvider<U>> ofProvider(
159                        PropertyFunction<LogProviderRef, LogProvider<U>, ? super Exception> mapper) {
160                return ofProviderRef().map(mapper);
161        }
162
163        /**
164         * Rewraps a value that was already derived from success's value, keeping the
165         * {@link PropertySuccess}'s origin (topProperties/properties/key/rawValue/kind)
166         * intact - useful for a conversion step that cannot itself throw, so
167         * {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)} would be overkill, but that still needs to
168         * keep the result's origin intact for a later conversion step's error message.
169         * @param <T> success's value type.
170         * @param <U> new value type.
171         * @param success success to take the origin from.
172         * @param value already-converted value to wrap.
173         * @return new success of the same shape as success, wrapping value.
174         */
175        static <T, U> Result.Success<U> mapValue(Result.Success<T> success, U value) {
176                return switch (success) {
177                        case PropertySuccess<T> ps ->
178                                new PropertySuccess<>(ps.topProperties(), ps.properties(), ps.key(), ps.rawValue(), ps.kind(), value);
179                };
180        }
181
182        /**
183         * Builds a rich error from a failed conversion of a previously successful result -
184         * package-visible (rather than private) only so the top-level {@link PropertySuccess}
185         * can call it from {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)}.
186         * @param <U> the converted value type.
187         * @param previousResult the success being converted.
188         * @param e the conversion failure.
189         * @return a rich error result.
190         */
191        static <U> Result.Error<U> richError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e) {
192                return richError(previousResult, e, "Error converting property");
193        }
194
195        /**
196         * Like {@link #richError(Result.Success, Exception)} but for a property whose value
197         * was used to invoke {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig)} rather than a
198         * plain same-property type conversion - see
199         * {@link #provideValue(Result, String, LogConfig)}. The provider constructs a
200         * genuinely separate component with its own property tree, so a failure inside it
201         * (typically already a complete, self-describing {@link ValidationException} of its
202         * own) must not be labeled "Error converting property": this property's own value
203         * converted just fine, it merely triggered a provider that failed on its own terms.
204         * @param <U> the provided component type.
205         * @param previousResult the success whose value was provided from.
206         * @param e the provisioning failure.
207         * @return a rich error result.
208         */
209        static <U> Result.Error<U> providingError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e) {
210                return richError(previousResult, e, "Failure providing from property");
211        }
212
213        /**
214         * Like {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)} but specifically for the "resolve to a
215         * {@link LogProvider}, then {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig) provide}"
216         * step used by output/encoder/appender resolution. A plain {@link Result#map} would
217         * relabel any failure from {@code provide(...)} as "Error converting property" even
218         * though this property's own value converted to a provider just fine - see
219         * {@link #providingError(Result.Success, Exception)}.
220         * @param <T> component type.
221         * @param providerResult an already-resolved provider, e.g. from
222         * {@link LogProperty#ofProvider(PropertyFunction)}.
223         * @param name component name passed to
224         * {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig)}.
225         * @param config config passed to {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig)}.
226         * @return the provided component, or the same {@link Result.Missing}/
227         * {@link Result.Error} a plain conversion would have produced.
228         */
229        static <T> Result<T> provideValue(Result<LogProvider<T>> providerResult, String name, LogConfig config) {
230                return switch (providerResult) {
231                        case Result.Success<LogProvider<T>> s -> {
232                                try {
233                                        yield mapValue(s, s.value().provide(name, config));
234                                }
235                                catch (Exception e) {
236                                        yield providingError(s, e);
237                                }
238                        }
239                        case Result.Missing<LogProvider<T>> m -> m.convert();
240                        case Result.Error<LogProvider<T>> e -> e.convert();
241                };
242        }
243
244        private static <U> Result.Error<U> richError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e, String chainedLabel) {
245                String fqk = previousResult.key();
246                PropertySuccess<?> ps = switch (previousResult) {
247                        case PropertySuccess<?> p -> p;
248                };
249                if (ps.kind() == PropertySuccess.Kind.VALUE) {
250                        String resolvedKey = ps.topProperties().description(fqk);
251                        String message = "Error for property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", " + e.getMessage();
252                        return new Result.Error<>(resolvedKey, message, e);
253                }
254                var badProps = ps.properties();
255                String badDescription = badProps.description(fqk);
256                String resolvedKey = "'" + fqk + "' from " + badDescription;
257                boolean chained = e instanceof PropertyConvertException || e instanceof ValidationException;
258                String own;
259                if (chained) {
260                        own = chainedLabel + ". key: " + resolvedKey + ", value: '" + ps.valueDescription() + "'";
261                }
262                else {
263                        String exceptionPrefix = e.getClass() == IllegalArgumentException.class ? "" : errorName(e) + " ";
264                        own = "Error for property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", " + exceptionPrefix + e.getMessage();
265                }
266                /*
267                 * Only worth a "Tried:" line if topProperties actually searched more broadly than
268                 * where the value was found (a chained/composite LogProperties) - for a
269                 * non-chained property, topProperties().description(fqk) is identical to
270                 * badDescription above, so appending it would just repeat the "key: ... from X"
271                 * text already shown on this exact message with nothing new to say.
272                 */
273                String triedDescription = ps.topProperties().description(fqk);
274                if (!triedDescription.equals(badDescription)) {
275                        String tried = "Tried: '" + fqk + "' from " + triedDescription;
276                        if (tried.length() > 120) {
277                                var sources = new ArrayList<String>();
278                                ps.topProperties().visit(fqk, (source, sourceKey) -> {
279                                        sources.add(source.description(sourceKey));
280                                        return null;
281                                });
282                                tried = "Tried:\n    '" + fqk + "' from:\n        " + String.join(",\n        ", sources);
283                        }
284                        own += "\n" + tried;
285                }
286                /*
287                 * Root cause first: e's own message already has everything beneath this layer
288                 * fully rendered (its own recursive "↳" trail included, if any), so this layer's
289                 * contribution is appended as one more arrow line rather than prepended - keeps
290                 * the deepest, most specific failure at the top no matter how many layers wrap
291                 * it. A non-chained e (a plain library exception like NumberFormatException) has
292                 * nothing beneath it to defer to, so its own message stays the whole (root) text.
293                 */
294                String message = chained ? e.getMessage() + "\n  ↳ " + own.replace("\n", "\n    ") : own;
295                return new Result.Error<>(resolvedKey, message, e);
296        }
297
298        /**
299         * Prefers {@link PropertyProblem#errorName()} (a short, stable name) over the
300         * exception's actual class name - a foreign exception (not one of ours) just gets its
301         * full class name as before.
302         */
303        private static String errorName(Exception e) {
304                if (e instanceof PropertyProblem pp) {
305                        return pp.errorName();
306                }
307                return e.getClass().getName();
308        }
309
310        /**
311         * Checks that value is not null, throwing {@link PropertyMissingException} naming key
312         * if it is. Useful for a property that is required but was set programmatically (e.g.
313         * a builder setter) rather than resolved through {@link #ofString()}/etc, so there is
314         * no {@link Result} to check for missing-ness.
315         * @param <T> value type.
316         * @param key property key, used only in the exception message.
317         * @param value value to check.
318         * @return value, never null.
319         * @throws PropertyMissingException if value is null.
320         */
321        static <T> T require(String key, @Nullable T value) {
322                if (value == null) {
323                        throw new PropertyMissingException("Value is required not null. property key='" + key + "'");
324                }
325                return value;
326        }
327
328        /**
329         * Adds a fallback key to try (without <code>{name}</code> interpolation) if none of
330         * the keys tried so far are found. Keys already added are tried first, in order; this
331         * one is tried last.
332         * @param fallbackKey additional key to try.
333         * @return a new LogProperty trying this key's keys followed by fallbackKey.
334         */
335        default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey) {
336                validateKey(fallbackKey);
337                return withKey(fallbackKey);
338        }
339
340        /**
341         * Adds a fallback key to try (with <code>{name}</code> interpolated to nameParam) if
342         * none of the keys tried so far are found.
343         * @param fallbackKey additional key to try, containing a <code>{name}</code>
344         * placeholder.
345         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code>.
346         * @return a new LogProperty trying this key's keys followed by fallbackKey.
347         */
348        default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey, String nameParam) {
349                String interpolated = LogProperties.interpolateNamedKey(fallbackKey, nameParam);
350                validateKey(interpolated);
351                return withKey(interpolated);
352        }
353
354        private LogProperty withKey(String fallbackKey) {
355                List<String> combined = new ArrayList<>(keys());
356                combined.add(fallbackKey);
357                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.copyOf(combined), properties());
358        }
359
360        /**
361         * Creates a LogProperty for a single key.
362         * @param properties properties this key will be looked up against.
363         * @param key key.
364         * @return LogProperty.
365         */
366        static LogProperty of(LogProperties properties, String key) {
367                validateKey(key);
368                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(key), properties);
369        }
370
371        /**
372         * Creates a LogProperty for a single key with a <code>{name}</code> parameter
373         * interpolated.
374         * @param properties properties this key will be looked up against.
375         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder.
376         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code>.
377         * @return LogProperty.
378         */
379        static LogProperty of(LogProperties properties, String key, String nameParam) {
380                String interpolated = LogProperties.interpolateNamedKey(key, nameParam);
381                validateKey(interpolated);
382                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(interpolated), properties);
383        }
384
385        /**
386         * Validates a fully resolved (post <code>{name}</code> interpolation) property key -
387         * must start with {@value LogProperties#ROOT_PREFIX}, must not start or end with
388         * {@value LogProperties#SEP}, and must not use a reserved key parameter name.
389         * @param key fully resolved key to validate.
390         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
391         */
392        private static void validateKey(String key) {
393                if (!key.startsWith(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX)) {
394                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
395                                        "Property key should start with: '" + LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX + "'. key = " + key);
396                }
397                if (key.endsWith(LogProperties.SEP) || key.startsWith(LogProperties.SEP)) {
398                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Property key should not start or end with '" + LogProperties.SEP + "'");
399                }
400                LogProperties.validateKeyParameters(key, Set.of());
401        }
402
403        /**
404         * An error friendly {@link Function} for converting properties.
405         *
406         * @param <T> input type.
407         * @param <R> output type.
408         * @param <E> error type.
409         */
410        public interface PropertyFunction<T extends @Nullable Object, R extends @Nullable Object, E extends Exception>
411                        extends Function<T, R> {
412
413                @Override
414                default R apply(T t) {
415                        try {
416                                return _apply(t);
417                        }
418                        catch (Exception e) {
419                                sneakyThrow(e);
420                                throw new RuntimeException(e);
421                        }
422                }
423
424                /**
425                 * Apply that throws error.
426                 * @param t input
427                 * @return output
428                 * @throws E if an error happened in function.
429                 */
430                public R _apply(T t) throws E;
431
432                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
433                private static <E extends Throwable> void sneakyThrow(final Throwable x) throws E {
434                        throw (E) x;
435                }
436
437        }
438
439        /**
440         * Parent interface for property exceptions.
441         */
442        sealed interface PropertyProblem permits PropertyConvertException, PropertyMissingException, ValidationException,
443                        LogProviderRef.NotFoundException {
444
445                /**
446                 * A short, stable name for this problem used in error messages instead of the
447                 * exception's full (and for a nested class, {@code $}-separated) class name.
448                 * Deliberately hardcoded per implementation rather than derived via
449                 * {@code getClass().getSimpleName()} so it stays stable across renames/moves of
450                 * the actual exception class.
451                 * @return error name.
452                 */
453                String errorName();
454
455        }
456
457        /**
458         * Property helper mixin.
459         */
460        interface PropertySupport {
461
462                /**
463                 * String key value properties.
464                 * @return properties.
465                 */
466                public LogProperties properties();
467
468        }
469
470        /**
471         * Thrown if an error happens while converting a property.
472         */
473        final static class PropertyConvertException extends RuntimeException implements PropertyProblem {
474
475                private static final long serialVersionUID = -6260241455268426342L;
476
477                /**
478                 * Key.
479                 */
480                private final String key;
481
482                /**
483                 * Creates convert exception.
484                 * @param key property key.
485                 * @param message error message
486                 * @param cause maybe null.
487                 */
488                PropertyConvertException(String key, String message, @Nullable Throwable cause) {
489                        super(message, cause);
490                        this.key = key;
491                }
492
493                /**
494                 * Property key.
495                 * @return key.
496                 */
497                public String key() {
498                        return this.key;
499                }
500
501                @Override
502                public String errorName() {
503                        return "PropertyConvertException";
504                }
505
506        }
507
508        /**
509         * Throw if property is missing.
510         */
511        final static class PropertyMissingException extends NoSuchElementException implements PropertyProblem {
512
513                private static final long serialVersionUID = 4203076848052565692L;
514
515                /**
516                 * Creates a missing property exception.
517                 * @param s error message.
518                 */
519                PropertyMissingException(String s) {
520                        super(s);
521                }
522
523                @Override
524                public String errorName() {
525                        return "PropertyMissingException";
526                }
527
528        }
529
530        /**
531         * Thrown by {@link Validator#validate()} when one or more of the accumulated
532         * {@link Result}s failed, reporting every failure in a single message instead of just
533         * the first one encountered.
534         */
535        final static class ValidationException extends RuntimeException implements PropertyProblem {
536
537                private static final long serialVersionUID = -8416817560218813225L;
538
539                ValidationException(String message, @Nullable Throwable cause) {
540                        super(message, cause);
541                }
542
543                @Override
544                public String errorName() {
545                        return "ValidationException";
546                }
547
548                /**
549                 * Validates a list of results and throws {@link ValidationException} if any
550                 * results are not {@link Result.Success}.
551                 * @param builder class to prefix to full message.
552                 * @param results list of results.
553                 * @throws ValidationException if any result in the supplied list is not
554                 * successful.
555                 */
556                public static void validate(Class<?> builder, List<Result<?>> results) throws ValidationException {
557                        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder().append("Validation failed for ")
558                                .append(builder.getName())
559                                .append(":");
560                        Throwable cause = null;
561                        boolean failed = false;
562                        for (var r : results) {
563                                switch (r) {
564                                        case Result.Success<?> s -> {
565                                                continue;
566                                        }
567                                        case Result.Missing<?> m -> {
568                                                sb.append("\n");
569                                                sb.append(m.message());
570                                                failed = true;
571                                        }
572                                        case Result.Error<?> e -> {
573                                                sb.append("\n");
574                                                sb.append(e.message());
575                                                if (cause == null) {
576                                                        cause = e.cause();
577                                                }
578                                                failed = true;
579                                        }
580                                }
581                        }
582                        if (failed) {
583                                throw new ValidationException(sb.toString(), cause);
584                        }
585
586                }
587
588                /**
589                 * Wraps cause in a {@link ValidationException}, using the same "Validation failed
590                 * for &lt;class&gt;:" message prefix {@link #validate(Class, List)} itself uses.
591                 * {@link ValidationException}'s constructor is package-private, so this is the
592                 * supported way for code outside this package - generated builder code in
593                 * particular - to report a downstream factory method's own defensive/cross-field
594                 * check (an {@link IllegalArgumentException}, say) through the same channel as a
595                 * per-field validation failure, without duplicating the message format itself.
596                 * Returns rather than throws so the caller writes
597                 * {@code throw ValidationException.of(...)} - keeps the throw itself, and
598                 * therefore unreachable-code/definite-assignment analysis at the call site,
599                 * visible there instead of hidden inside this method.
600                 * @param builder class to prefix to the message, same role as
601                 * {@link #validate(Class, List)}'s own parameter.
602                 * @param cause the exception to wrap.
603                 * @return a new {@link ValidationException} wrapping cause; not thrown by this
604                 * method.
605                 */
606                public static ValidationException of(Class<?> builder, RuntimeException cause) {
607                        return new ValidationException("Validation failed for " + builder.getName() + ": " + cause.getMessage(),
608                                        cause);
609                }
610
611        }
612
613        /**
614         * Accumulates {@link Result}s from one or more property lookups and validates them
615         * together, so that a caller resolving several properties in sequence can report
616         * every failure at once instead of failing fast on the first bad property.
617         * <p>
618         * This is the mechanism generated {@code fromProperties(LogProperties)} builder
619         * implementations use: each property is looked up and its {@link Result} is added to
620         * the validator as it is read; {@link #validate()} is then called once at the end,
621         * after all properties have been read, so a user who misconfigured several properties
622         * sees all of the problems together rather than fixing them one at a time across
623         * repeated runs.
624         * <p>
625         * Use {@link #add(Result)} for a property that is required: a {@link Result.Missing}
626         * is treated as a failure. Use {@link #addIfError(Result)} for an optional property
627         * that already has a fallback applied (typically via {@link Result#or(Object)} with
628         * the builder's current field value): a {@link Result.Missing} is expected in that
629         * case and is silently ignored, but a {@link Result.Error} (the property was present
630         * but failed to convert) is still a real problem and is reported.
631         *
632         * @apiNote a {@code Validator} is single-use: create one with {@link #of(Class)}, add
633         * every result that should be checked, and call {@link #validate()} exactly once at
634         * the end.
635         */
636        public static class Validator {
637
638                private final List<Result<?>> results = new ArrayList<>();
639
640                private final Class<?> builder;
641
642                /**
643                 * Creates a validator whose {@link ValidationException} messages will be prefixed
644                 * with the name of the given class.
645                 * @param builder the class on whose behalf properties are being resolved -
646                 * typically the builder calling this method. It is only used to identify the
647                 * source of a failure in the exception message; no state is read from it.
648                 * @return newly created validator.
649                 */
650                public static Validator of(Class<?> builder) {
651                        return new Validator(builder);
652                }
653
654                private Validator(Class<?> builder) {
655                        this.builder = builder;
656                }
657
658                /**
659                 * Adds a result that must be present. Both {@link Result.Missing} and
660                 * {@link Result.Error} will cause {@link #validate()} to fail. Use this for a
661                 * required property; for an optional property that already has a fallback value
662                 * applied, use {@link #addIfError(Result)} instead so a missing value does not
663                 * itself trigger a failure.
664                 * @param result result to check.
665                 * @return this.
666                 */
667                public Validator add(Result<?> result) {
668                        results.add(result);
669                        return this;
670                }
671
672                /**
673                 * Adds a result only if it is a {@link Result.Error}; a {@link Result.Missing}
674                 * result is silently ignored. Intended for an optional property that has already
675                 * had a fallback value applied (for example via {@link Result#or(Object)}): the
676                 * property being absent is expected and fine, but if it was present and failed to
677                 * convert that should not be swallowed.
678                 * @param result result to check.
679                 * @return this.
680                 */
681                public Validator addIfError(Result<?> result) {
682                        if (result instanceof Result.Error<?> e) {
683                                results.add(e);
684                        }
685                        return this;
686                }
687
688                /**
689                 * Validates every result added so far via {@link #add(Result)} or
690                 * {@link #addIfError(Result)}, throwing a single exception listing all failures
691                 * if one or more of them are not {@link Result.Success}.
692                 * @throws ValidationException if any added result is a {@link Result.Missing}
693                 * (added via {@link #add(Result)}) or a {@link Result.Error} (added via either
694                 * method).
695                 */
696                public void validate() throws ValidationException {
697                        ValidationException.validate(builder, results);
698                }
699
700                /**
701                 * Validates every name in a list resolved from a comma-separated list property
702                 * (e.g. appenders/routes) before any of those names are used to construct
703                 * anything, so a bad name is reported against the list property itself rather
704                 * than against whatever unrelated {@code {name}}-keyed property a downstream
705                 * lookup happens to interpolate first. Static (rather than an instance method
706                 * using an existing {@link Validator}'s own {@code builder} field) since this
707                 * check is independent of - and never participates in - whatever else a
708                 * particular {@link Validator} instance may have accumulated via
709                 * {@link #add(Result)}/{@link #addIfError(Result)}.
710                 * @param component the class on whose behalf these names are being resolved -
711                 * used to prefix the thrown {@link ValidationException}'s message, the same role
712                 * {@link #of(Class)} plays elsewhere.
713                 * @param kind short noun describing what these names are (e.g.
714                 * {@code "appender"}, {@code "route"}), used only for the message.
715                 * @param source the result the list itself was resolved from, used only for its
716                 * {@link Result#describe()} in the message.
717                 * @param names names to validate.
718                 * @return names unchanged if all are valid.
719                 * @throws ValidationException if any name is blank or has other characters.
720                 */
721                static List<String> validateNames(Class<?> component, String kind, Result<?> source, List<String> names) {
722                        for (String name : names) {
723                                if (!isValidName(name)) {
724                                        throw ValidationException.of(component,
725                                                        new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid " + kind + " name '" + name + "' in "
726                                                                        + source.describe() + ": must be alphanumeric (hyphen/underscore allowed)"));
727                                }
728                        }
729                        return names;
730                }
731
732                /**
733                 * Validates that a key parameter token (the identifier inside <code>{...}</code>
734                 * in a key template, e.g. <code>"name"</code> in <code>a.{name}.b</code>) is well
735                 * formed: non-blank and made up only of letters, digits, <code>-</code>, or
736                 * <code>_</code>. This guards against a malformed key <em>template</em>, not user
737                 * input.
738                 * @param parameter parameter token found in a key template.
739                 * @return the parameter unchanged if valid.
740                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the parameter is blank or has other
741                 * characters.
742                 */
743                static String validateKeyParameter(String parameter) {
744                        if (!isValidName(parameter)) {
745                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
746                                                "Key parameter must be alphanumeric (hyphen/underscore allowed). parameter: '" + parameter
747                                                                + "'");
748                        }
749                        return parameter;
750                }
751
752                /**
753                 * Validates that a value about to be interpolated for a <code>{name}</code>-style
754                 * key parameter is well formed: non-blank and made up only of letters, digits,
755                 * <code>-</code>, or <code>_</code>. This is the single choke point every
756                 * keyed-name mechanism in the project (appender/output/encoder/publisher/route
757                 * names, and every annotation-processor generated builder's own property prefix)
758                 * funnels through via {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Function)}.
759                 * @param key original, pre-interpolation key template (e.g.
760                 * <code>a.{name}.b</code>).
761                 * @param parameter name of the parameter being interpolated (e.g.
762                 * <code>"name"</code>).
763                 * @param value value about to be substituted for the parameter.
764                 * @return the value unchanged if valid.
765                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the value is blank or has other characters.
766                 */
767                static String validateKeyParameterValue(String key, String parameter, String value) {
768                        validateKeyParameter(parameter);
769                        if (!isValidName(value)) {
770                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("\"" + key + "\" cannot be interpolated: parameter '" + parameter
771                                                + "' value '" + value + "' must be alphanumeric (hyphen/underscore allowed)");
772                        }
773                        return value;
774                }
775
776                private static boolean isValidName(String s) {
777                        if (s.isBlank()) {
778                                return false;
779                        }
780                        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
781                                char c = s.charAt(i);
782                                if (!Character.isLetterOrDigit(c) && c != '-' && c != '_') {
783                                        return false;
784                                }
785                        }
786                        return true;
787                }
788
789        }
790
791        /**
792         * The result of a property fetched from properties.
793         *
794         * @param <T> property type.
795         */
796        sealed interface Result<T> {
797
798                /**
799                 * Registers this result with {@code validator} via {@link Validator#add(Result)}
800                 * (a still-{@link Missing} result is treated as a real failure) and returns this
801                 * result unchanged, so a chain that builds a required property can register
802                 * itself with a shared {@link Validator} and keep going in one expression -
803                 * {@code properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validate(v)} - instead of
804                 * a separate {@code var x = ...; v.add(x);} statement pair. The validator is
805                 * shared and single-use by design: add every property's result this way (or via
806                 * {@link #validateIfError(Validator)} for an optional one), then call
807                 * {@link Validator#validate()} exactly once at the end to report every failure
808                 * together instead of one exception per property.
809                 * @param validator validator to add this result to.
810                 * @return this result, unchanged.
811                 */
812                default ValidatedResult<T> validate(Validator validator) {
813                        validator.add(this);
814                        return (ValidatedResult<T>) this;
815                }
816
817                /**
818                 * Like {@link #validate(Validator)} but via {@link Validator#addIfError(Result)}
819                 * instead of {@link Validator#add(Result)} - a {@link Missing} result is expected
820                 * and ignored, only a {@link Result.Error} is treated as a failure. Intended for
821                 * an optional property that already has a fallback applied (for example via
822                 * {@link #or(Object)}): the property being absent is fine, but if it was present
823                 * and failed to convert that should not be swallowed.
824                 * @param validator validator to add this result to.
825                 * @return this result, unchanged.
826                 */
827                default ValidatedResult<T> validateIfError(Validator validator) {
828                        validator.addIfError(this);
829                        return (ValidatedResult<T>) this;
830                }
831
832                /**
833                 * Convenience for a genuine one-off, single-property validation that does not
834                 * need to participate in a larger batch: builds a single-use {@link Validator},
835                 * registers this result with it via {@link Validator#add(Result)}, and validates
836                 * immediately - instead of registering with a caller-managed {@link Validator}
837                 * via {@link #validate(Validator)} and deferring to a later
838                 * {@link Validator#validate()} call.
839                 * <p>
840                 * Uses {@link Validator#add(Result)} semantics: a still-{@link Missing} result is
841                 * treated as a failure, same as an absent required property with no fallback. If
842                 * this property is optional, apply a fallback first -
843                 * {@code properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validateNow(component)} -
844                 * since a result with a fallback applied is never {@link Missing}. For a property
845                 * that should tolerate being missing but not being present-and-malformed, use
846                 * {@link #validateIfError(Validator)} with an externally-owned {@link Validator}
847                 * instead - there is deliberately no addIfError-equivalent of this method, to
848                 * avoid two same-named single-property convenience methods with silently
849                 * different failure semantics.
850                 * @param component the class on whose behalf this property is being resolved -
851                 * only used to name the source of the failure in the exception message.
852                 * @return value.
853                 * @throws ValidationException if this result is not a {@link Success}.
854                 */
855                default T validateNow(Class<?> component) {
856                        var v = Validator.of(component);
857                        v.add(this);
858                        v.validate();
859                        var result = switch (this) {
860                                case ValidatedResult<T> vr -> vr;
861                        };
862                        return result.value();
863                }
864
865                /**
866                 * Returns the current result if fallback is null or returns fallback as a result
867                 * if this result is missing.
868                 * @param fallback maybe <code>null</code>.
869                 * @return value.
870                 */
871                public Result<T> or(@Nullable T fallback);
872
873                /**
874                 * Returns the current result if success or error otherwise fallback supplier is
875                 * used. If the supplier returns <code>null</code> then the result will be mising.
876                 * @param fallback may return <code>null</code> but not recommended.
877                 * @return value.
878                 */
879                public Result<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback);
880
881                /**
882                 * Maps this result's value through {@code mapper}. On success, keeps the origin
883                 * ({@link PropertySuccess#topProperties() topProperties}/properties/key/
884                 * rawValue/kind, see {@link PropertySuccess}) so a later conversion step's error
885                 * message can still point back to it. On failure, builds a rich error message -
886                 * which key it came from, where that key was found, and (for
887                 * {@link PropertyConvertException}/{@link ValidationException} causes) the
888                 * original raw value - with a "Tried:" line searching {@code topProperties}: the
889                 * {@link LogProperties} the very first {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} in
890                 * this chain was looked up against, which for a chained/composite
891                 * {@code LogProperties.of(a, b)} can be broader than the exact source the value
892                 * was actually found at. Usable at any point in a chain, not just directly off a
893                 * {@link LogProperty}, since a {@link Success} keeps pointing back to the
894                 * property it originally came from no matter how many conversions have run since.
895                 * @param <U> result type
896                 * @param mapper mapping function.
897                 * @return mapped result.
898                 */
899                public <U> Result<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper);
900
901                /**
902                 * A description of the result for error messages.
903                 * @return description.
904                 */
905                public String describe();
906
907                /**
908                 * A property that is present.
909                 *
910                 * @param <T> property type.
911                 */
912                public sealed interface Success<T> extends RequiredResult<T> permits PropertySuccess {
913
914                        @Override
915                        default @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
916                                return value();
917                        }
918
919                        /**
920                         * Gets the value and will never fail for Success.
921                         * @return value.
922                         */
923                        @Override
924                        public T value();
925
926                        @Override
927                        default Success<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
928                                return this;
929                        }
930
931                        @Override
932                        default Success<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
933                                return this;
934                        }
935
936                        /**
937                         * Original property key where the value was derived from or was passed a
938                         * fallback.
939                         * @return key.
940                         */
941                        public String key();
942
943                }
944
945                /**
946                 * A property that is missing (<code>null</code>).
947                 *
948                 * @param <T> property type.
949                 * @param properties the properties that were searched, kept around so
950                 * {@link #or(Object)} can hand it to the {@link PropertySuccess} it builds for a
951                 * supplied fallback.
952                 * @param keys keys.
953                 * @param message description of where the property is missing.
954                 */
955                public record Missing<T>(LogProperties properties, List<String> keys,
956                                String message) implements ValidatedResult<T> {
957                        /**
958                         * A property that is missing (<code>null</code>).
959                         * @param properties the properties that were searched.
960                         * @param keys keys.
961                         * @param message description of where the property is missing.
962                         */
963                        public Missing {
964                                if (keys.isEmpty()) {
965                                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("one key is required");
966                                }
967                        }
968
969                        @Override
970                        public @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
971                                return null;
972                        }
973
974                        @Override
975                        public T value() throws NoSuchElementException {
976                                throw new PropertyMissingException(message);
977                        }
978
979                        @Override
980                        public Result<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
981                                if (fallback != null) {
982                                        return new PropertySuccess<>(properties, properties, keys.get(0), fallback,
983                                                        PropertySuccess.Kind.VALUE, fallback);
984                                }
985                                return this;
986                        }
987
988                        @Override
989                        public Result<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
990                                return or(fallback.get());
991                        }
992
993                        /**
994                         * Helper just to cast the result to a different parameterized type.
995                         * @param <R> parameterized type.
996                         * @return this.
997                         */
998                        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
999                        public <R> Missing<R> convert() {
1000                                return (Missing<R>) this;
1001                        }
1002
1003                        @Override
1004                        public <U> Missing<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1005                                return convert();
1006                        }
1007
1008                        @Override
1009                        public String describe() {
1010                                return "Missing[" + keys + "]";
1011                        }
1012
1013                }
1014
1015                /**
1016                 * A property that was present but failed conversion.
1017                 *
1018                 * @param <T> property type.
1019                 * @param key property key that failed to convert.
1020                 * @param message failure message.
1021                 * @param cause exception thrown while trying to convert.
1022                 */
1023                @SuppressWarnings("JavaLangClash")
1024                public record Error<T>(String key, String message, Exception cause) implements ValidatedResult<T> {
1025                        /*
1026                         * TODO consider rename to Failure
1027                         */
1028                        @Override
1029                        public @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
1030                                throw new PropertyConvertException(key, message, cause);
1031                        }
1032
1033                        @Override
1034                        public T value() throws PropertyConvertException {
1035                                throw new PropertyConvertException(key, message, cause);
1036                        }
1037
1038                        @Override
1039                        public Error<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
1040                                return this;
1041                        }
1042
1043                        @Override
1044                        public Error<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
1045                                return this;
1046                        }
1047
1048                        /**
1049                         * Helper just to cast the result to a different parameterized type.
1050                         * @param <R> parameterized type.
1051                         * @return this.
1052                         */
1053                        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
1054                        public <R> Error<R> convert() {
1055                                return (Error<R>) this;
1056                        }
1057
1058                        @Override
1059                        public <U> Error<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1060                                return convert();
1061                        }
1062
1063                        @Override
1064                        public String describe() {
1065                                return "Error[" + key + "](" + message + ")";
1066                        }
1067                }
1068
1069        }
1070
1071        /**
1072         * A {@link Result} that is safe to pull a value out of - either because it can never
1073         * actually be missing ({@link RequiredResult}: a {@link Success} or an
1074         * {@link Result.Error}, both already resolved one way or the other) or because a
1075         * caller has explicitly acknowledged the possibility of a still-{@link Missing}
1076         * result by running it through {@link Result#validate(Validator)},
1077         * {@link Result#validateIfError(Validator)}, or {@link Result#validateNow(Class)}.
1078         * <p>
1079         * {@link Result} itself deliberately does not declare {@link #value()}/
1080         * {@link #valueOrNull()}/{@link #optional()} - a bare {@link Result} returned by
1081         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()} and friends forces a caller through one of those
1082         * validation paths before it can pull a value out, instead of blindly calling
1083         * {@code value()} on a result that might still be {@link Missing}.
1084         *
1085         * @param <T> property type.
1086         */
1087        sealed interface ValidatedResult<T> extends Result<T> {
1088
1089                /**
1090                 * Gets the value and will fail with {@link NoSuchElementException} if there is no
1091                 * value.
1092                 * @return value.
1093                 * @throws PropertyMissingException if there is no value.
1094                 * @throws PropertyConvertException if the property failed conversion.
1095                 */
1096                public T value() throws PropertyMissingException, PropertyConvertException;
1097
1098                /**
1099                 * Gets the value.
1100                 * @return value or <code>null</code>.
1101                 */
1102                public @Nullable T valueOrNull();
1103
1104                /**
1105                 * Gets a value if there is if not uses the fallback.
1106                 * @param fallback maybe <code>null</code>.
1107                 * @return value.
1108                 */
1109                default @Nullable T valueOrNull(@Nullable T fallback) {
1110                        var v = valueOrNull();
1111                        if (v != null) {
1112                                return v;
1113                        }
1114                        return fallback;
1115                }
1116
1117                /**
1118                 * Convenience that turns a value into an optional.
1119                 * @return optional.
1120                 */
1121                default Optional<T> optional() {
1122                        return Optional.ofNullable(valueOrNull());
1123                }
1124
1125        }
1126
1127        /**
1128         * A result that is not missing and will either be an error or success.
1129         *
1130         * @param <T> property type.
1131         */
1132        sealed interface RequiredResult<T> extends ValidatedResult<T> {
1133
1134        }
1135
1136}
1137
1138/**
1139 * A property that is present, either because it was actually found in properties, or
1140 * (when {@code kind} is {@link Kind#VALUE}) because it was missing there and a fallback
1141 * value was supplied instead.
1142 * <p>
1143 * Not public: nothing outside {@code LogProperty}'s own resolution machinery (in this
1144 * package) constructs or pattern-matches on this directly - callers work through the
1145 * sealed {@link LogProperty.Result}/{@link LogProperty.Result.Success} interfaces
1146 * instead.
1147 *
1148 * @param <T> property type.
1149 * @param topProperties the {@link LogProperties} the very first
1150 * {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} in this chain was looked up against - for a
1151 * chained/composite {@code LogProperties.of(a, b)} this is the whole composite, not just
1152 * whichever member the value ended up found in. Used for a failure message's "Tried:"
1153 * line, which can therefore search more broadly than {@code properties}.
1154 * @param properties the properties searched; for {@link Kind#STRING}/{@link Kind#LIST}/
1155 * {@link Kind#MAP} the <strong>exact</strong> properties where the value was found - for
1156 * a chained/composite search this can be narrower than {@code topProperties}, naming just
1157 * the one member the value was actually found in. Used for a failure message's "key: ...
1158 * from X" line.
1159 * @param key property key.
1160 * @param rawValue value as originally found (or the fallback, for {@link Kind#VALUE}),
1161 * before any conversion - a {@link String}, {@link List List&lt;String&gt;}, or
1162 * {@link Map Map&lt;String,String&gt;} depending on kind.
1163 * @param kind which of {@link LogProperty}'s {@code ofString()}/{@code ofList()}/
1164 * {@code ofMap()} this property was found through, and so rawValue's runtime type - or
1165 * {@link Kind#VALUE} if it was not found at all and rawValue is a fallback.
1166 * @param value actual (possibly converted) value.
1167 * @apiNote rawValue/kind stick around after a conversion (e.g.
1168 * {@link LogProperty#ofInt()} converting the string this was found as into an
1169 * {@code Integer}) so error messages can still describe the original value - value's type
1170 * and rawValue's kind are not always in sync.
1171 */
1172record PropertySuccess<T>(LogProperties topProperties, LogProperties properties, String key, Object rawValue,
1173                PropertySuccess.Kind kind, T value) implements LogProperty.Result.Success<T> {
1174
1175        /**
1176         * Which of {@link LogProperty}'s typed accessors a {@link PropertySuccess} was found
1177         * through, and so what {@link PropertySuccess#rawValue()}'s runtime type actually is
1178         * - or that it was not found at all and is a plain fallback value.
1179         */
1180        enum Kind {
1181
1182                /**
1183                 * rawValue is a {@link String}, found via {@link LogProperty#ofString()}.
1184                 */
1185                STRING,
1186                /**
1187                 * rawValue is a {@link List List&lt;String&gt;}, found via
1188                 * {@link LogProperty#ofList()}.
1189                 */
1190                LIST,
1191                /**
1192                 * rawValue is a {@link Map Map&lt;String,String&gt;}, found via
1193                 * {@link LogProperty#ofMap()}.
1194                 */
1195                MAP,
1196                /**
1197                 * Not found in properties at all - rawValue is a plain fallback value supplied
1198                 * via {@link LogProperty.Result#or}.
1199                 */
1200                VALUE
1201
1202        }
1203
1204        /**
1205         * Successfully found property value.
1206         * @param topProperties the properties the original lookup started from.
1207         * @param properties the properties searched.
1208         * @param key property key.
1209         * @param rawValue value as originally found (or the fallback), before any conversion.
1210         * @param kind rawValue's kind.
1211         * @param value actual value should not be <code>null</code>.
1212         */
1213        PropertySuccess {
1214                if (value == null) {
1215                        throw new NullPointerException("value");
1216                }
1217        }
1218
1219        @Override
1220        public <U> LogProperty.Result<U> map(LogProperty.PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1221                try {
1222                        U u = mapper._apply(value);
1223                        return new PropertySuccess<>(topProperties, properties, key, rawValue, kind, u);
1224                }
1225                catch (Exception e) {
1226                        return LogProperty.richError(this, e);
1227                }
1228        }
1229
1230        @Override
1231        public String describe() {
1232                if (kind == Kind.VALUE) {
1233                        return "Fallback[" + key + "]=" + LogRedactor.redactProperty(key, String.valueOf(value));
1234                }
1235                return "Property[" + key + "]=" + valueDescription();
1236        }
1237
1238        String valueDescription() {
1239                String s = kind == Kind.STRING ? (String) rawValue : String.valueOf(rawValue);
1240                return LogRedactor.redactProperty(key, s);
1241        }
1242
1243}
1244
1245final class LogRedactor {
1246
1247        private LogRedactor() {
1248        }
1249
1250        private static final Set<String> REDACTED_KEYS = Set.of("password", "apikey", "secret", "token", "passwd",
1251                        "passphrase", "credential", "privatekey", "accesskey", "authorization");
1252
1253        private static final String REDACTED_VALUE = "<REDACTED>";
1254
1255        static String redactProperty(String key, String input) {
1256                if (sensitiveKey(key)) {
1257                        return REDACTED_VALUE;
1258                }
1259                if (input.indexOf('?') < 0 && input.indexOf('@') < 0) {
1260                        return input;
1261                }
1262                try {
1263                        return redactUri(new URI(input));
1264                }
1265                catch (URISyntaxException e) {
1266                        return input;
1267                }
1268        }
1269
1270        private static boolean sensitiveKey(String key) {
1271                String normalizedKey = key.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).replace(".", "").replace("_", "").replace("-", "");
1272                for (var k : REDACTED_KEYS) {
1273                        if (normalizedKey.contains(k)) {
1274                                return true;
1275                        }
1276                }
1277                return false;
1278        }
1279
1280        static String redactUri(URI uri) {
1281                String source = uri.toString();
1282                var result = new StringBuilder(source);
1283                String query = uri.getRawQuery();
1284                if (query != null) {
1285                        int queryStart = source.indexOf('?') + 1;
1286                        result.replace(queryStart, queryStart + query.length(), redactQuery(query));
1287                }
1288                String authority = uri.getRawAuthority();
1289                if (authority != null) {
1290                        int userInfoEnd = authority.lastIndexOf('@');
1291                        if (userInfoEnd >= 0) {
1292                                String scheme = uri.getScheme();
1293                                int authorityStart = scheme == null ? 2 : scheme.length() + 3;
1294                                result.replace(authorityStart, authorityStart + userInfoEnd, REDACTED_VALUE);
1295                        }
1296                }
1297                return result.toString();
1298        }
1299
1300        private static String redactQuery(String query) {
1301                var result = new StringBuilder();
1302                int start = 0;
1303                for (int i = 0; i <= query.length(); i++) {
1304                        if (i == query.length() || query.charAt(i) == '&' || query.charAt(i) == ',') {
1305                                String pair = query.substring(start, i);
1306                                int equals = pair.indexOf('=');
1307                                if (equals >= 0) {
1308                                        String key = pair.substring(0, equals);
1309                                        String decodedKey = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1310                                        result.append(key)
1311                                                .append('=')
1312                                                .append(sensitiveKey(decodedKey) ? REDACTED_VALUE : pair.substring(equals + 1));
1313                                }
1314                                else {
1315                                        result.append(pair);
1316                                }
1317                                if (i < query.length()) {
1318                                        result.append(query.charAt(i));
1319                                }
1320                                start = i + 1;
1321                        }
1322                }
1323                return result.toString();
1324        }
1325
1326}
1327
1328final class DefaultLogProperty implements LogProperty {
1329
1330        private final List<String> keys;
1331
1332        private final LogProperties properties;
1333
1334        DefaultLogProperty(List<String> keys, LogProperties properties) {
1335                super();
1336                if (keys.isEmpty()) {
1337                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("at least one key is required");
1338                }
1339                this.keys = keys;
1340                this.properties = properties;
1341        }
1342
1343        @Override
1344        public String key() {
1345                return keys.get(0);
1346        }
1347
1348        @Override
1349        public List<String> keys() {
1350                return keys;
1351        }
1352
1353        @Override
1354        public LogProperties properties() {
1355                return this.properties;
1356        }
1357
1358        @Override
1359        public Result<String> ofString() {
1360                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1361                        var v = p.valueOrNull(kk);
1362                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.STRING, v);
1363                }));
1364        }
1365
1366        @Override
1367        public Result<List<String>> ofList() {
1368                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1369                        var v = p.listOrNull(kk);
1370                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.LIST, v);
1371                }));
1372        }
1373
1374        @Override
1375        public Result<Map<String, String>> ofMap() {
1376                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1377                        var v = p.mapOrNull(kk);
1378                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.MAP, v);
1379                }));
1380        }
1381
1382        private <T> Result<T> resolve(java.util.function.Function<String, Result.@Nullable Success<T>> lookup) {
1383                for (String k : keys) {
1384                        var success = lookup.apply(k);
1385                        if (success != null) {
1386                                return success;
1387                        }
1388                }
1389                return missingResult(properties, keys);
1390        }
1391
1392        <T> Result.Missing<T> missingResult(LogProperties props, List<String> keys) {
1393                List<String> resolvedKeys = describeKeys(props, keys);
1394                String label = keys.size() == 1 ? "key" : "keys";
1395                String message = "Property missing. " + label + ": " + resolvedKeys;
1396                if (message.length() > 120) {
1397                        var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
1398                        for (var key : keys) {
1399                                String fqk = fullyQualifiedKey(key);
1400                                var sources = new ArrayList<String>();
1401                                props.visit(fqk, (source, sourceKey) -> {
1402                                        sources.add(source.description(sourceKey));
1403                                        return null;
1404                                });
1405                                descriptions.add("'" + fqk + "' from:\n        " + String.join(",\n        ", sources));
1406                        }
1407                        message = "Property missing. " + label + ":\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
1408                }
1409                return new Result.Missing<>(props, keys, message);
1410        }
1411
1412        List<String> describeKeys(LogProperties props, List<String> keys) {
1413                return keys.stream().<String>map(k -> {
1414                        String fqk = fullyQualifiedKey(k);
1415                        return "'" + fqk + "' from " + props.description(fullyQualifiedKey(k));
1416                }).toList();
1417        }
1418
1419        String fullyQualifiedKey(String key) {
1420                return key;
1421        }
1422
1423}
